title: Chapter 7 bankruptcy - basics
facts: Chapter 7 is a federal bankruptcy process involving liquidation rules and can provide eligible individual debtors a discharge of many debts.
A Chapter 7 trustee administers the case and may liquidate nonexempt property for creditors, while exempt property can be protected under applicable exemption law.
Many individual Chapter 7 cases are no-asset cases in which there are no nonexempt assets available for distribution, but this depends on the debtor's property and exemptions.
Chapter 7 does not discharge every type of debt and does not automatically eliminate valid liens on property.
